Question 1
?

The entry a13′ in the inverse of the matrix A=[02−12k1014] equals 118 and det(A)=−18. Find the value of k.

a
1
b
3
c
2
d
−1
e
−3
Submit

decision.explanation: The inverse entry a′₁₃ equals C₃₁/det(A). Here C₃₁ = det([[2,-1],[k,1]]) = 2+k. Thus (2+k)/(-18)=1/18, giving 2+k=-1 and k=-3.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
The entry ${a}_{13}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & k & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]$
equals $\frac{1}{18}$ and $det(A)=-18.$ Find the value of $k.$
after.worked_solution:
First, note that we are given the determinant of $A:$

$$
det(A)=-18
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{13}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{31}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{31} & =(-1)^{3+1}|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ k & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ k & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2+k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{13}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{31} \\  & =-\frac{1}{18}\cdot (2+k).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{13}^{′}=\frac{1}{18}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{18}(2+k) & =\frac{1}{18} \\ 2+k & =-1 \\ k & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

The entry a32′ in the inverse of the matrix A=[10111k−121] equals −1 and det(A)=4−2k. Find the value of k.

a
0
b
1
c
−1
d
2
e
−2
Submit

decision.explanation: The inverse entry a′₃₂ is C₂₃/det(A). Its cofactor is C₂₃ = −det([[1,0],[-1,2]]) = −2. Thus −2/(4−2k) = −1, so 4−2k = 2 and k = 1. The determinant is then 2, so the inverse exists.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
The entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & k \\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]$
equals $-1$ and $det(A)=4-2k.$ Find the value of $k.$
after.worked_solution:
First, note that we are given the determinant of $A:$

$$
det(A)=4-2k
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{23}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{23} & =(-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(2-0) \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{32}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{23} \\  & =\frac{1}{4-2k}\cdot (-2) \\  & =\frac{1}{k-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{32}^{′}=-1$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{k-2} & =-1 \\ 1 & =2-k \\ k & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
